name: HarmBench
description: A standardized evaluation framework for automated red-teaming and jailbreak assessment, benchmarking 18 red-teaming methods against 33 LLMs across approximately 510 harmful behavior categories. Provides standardized, reproducible Attack Success Rate (ASR) metrics, enabling fair comparison of jailbreak attack and defense methods across models.
evaluation_method: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — fraction of harmful behaviors successfully elicited
typical_sota_score: Varies by attack method and model; best defenses achieve <5% ASR on most attacks
reputation: De facto standard for jailbreak evaluation; developed by Center for AI Safety (CAIS); used by US and UK AI Safety Institutes; published as a major safety benchmark in 2024; widely cited in safety research
notes: Released February 2024. Tests 18 attack methods including GCG, PEZ, PAIR, TAP, and others. Categories span cybersecurity, weapons, harassment, and misinformation. Used by US AISI and UK AISI for pre-deployment testing. Complemented by JailbreakBench (UPenn/ETH/EPFL, NeurIPS 2024). Provides a standardized, reproducible framework that prior work lacked.
